# Changelog

Notable changes to this repository are recorded here from 02/09/2026 onward.
Earlier work is verifiable in the commit history and in the closed pull
requests.

This repository is **not versioned**: it publishes the personal profile of
`lcv-leo` and the static site at lcv-leo.lcv.dev. It does not publish packages
or a numbered artifact. Entries are grouped by date rather than semantic
version. Dates are written `DD/MM/AAAA` in Brasília time (UTC−03:00).

## Unreleased

- Adopt the GitHub Actions workflow dependency lockfile
  (`.github/workflows/actions.lock`, generated by `gh actions-lock --no-narrow`),
  which records every action dependency at an exact commit together with the
  source repository identity, and is refreshed by Dependabot in the same pull
  request
  ([Workflow dependency lockfiles](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles)).
  Every workflow `uses:` reference keeps its full-length commit SHA and version
  comment unchanged; the lockfile adds pinning for the three transitive Action
  revisions the workflow files cannot express (`oven-sh/setup-bun` v2.2.0,
  `actions/upload-artifact` v7.0.0 and `github/codeql-action` v4.39.3), now
  named with their commits and commit-pinned license links in the new
  `THIRDPARTY.md` subsection. The `Require lockfile` policy runs in **Evaluate**
  mode at the enterprise. This
  repository has no same-repository `uses: ./` action, so neither
  `--migrate-local-actions` nor `--ignore-local-actions` applies. `AGENTS.md`
  and `CLAUDE.md` Sections 6.E item 2 and 7.A now copy the workspace master
  text that adopts the lockfile, replacing the passages that declared it
  nonexistent or retired, and `SECURITY.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the
  third-party inventory carry the same rule; the inventory's license links for
  `github/codeql-action`, `zizmorcore/zizmor-action` and
  `anthropics/claude-code-action` were aligned to the pins the workflow files
  already carry (LCV-719).

- Run the official `verify-lockfile` workflow
  (`.github/workflows/verify-lockfile.yml`) on every pull request through the
  `github/gh-actions-lock` action, pinned to `verify/v0.5.1` at its full commit
  SHA. The job fails when `.github/workflows/actions.lock` is out of sync with
  the workflow files or a locked pin no longer verifies upstream, so drift is
  visible on the pull request that introduces it. The check reports and does not
  block: it is not a required check (LCV-738).

- Update Claude Code Action to v1.0.280 and Dependency Review Action to v5.0.1
  at their complete immutable release commit SHAs, preserving workflow inputs
  and permissions. Align the Claude Code Action MIT license link with its new
  pin; the bundled minimatch license change to ISC is approved under LCV-666.

# Third-party components

This inventory covers every external GitHub Action invoked by the repository
workflows, the CI-only npm and browser validation tooling, and the externally
hosted components used by the profile or the Pages site. The repository's
package manifest contains only development tooling for browser-level
provenance tests. No npm package, browser binary, or FFmpeg binary is copied
into `site/` or the deployed GitHub Pages artifact; the site's committed
JavaScript uses browser built-ins and GitHub APIs.

The versioned inventory is the repository's **dependency graph** (Insights →
Dependency graph), which GitHub maintains from the committed manifest, lockfile
and workflow files and exports as an SBOM on request. Versions, version ranges
and immutable commit pins for everything a workflow references directly live
only in `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, the workflow files and
`.github/workflows/actions.lock`, where Dependabot updates them; this document
does not restate those direct pins, so it can never drift from those sources.
The single exception is the transitive Action revisions that no
workflow `uses:` line points at: their exact commits are named in the
subsection under **GitHub
Actions** below, because no workflow reference records them. The
GitHub Actions dependency lockfile (`.github/workflows/actions.lock`, generated
by `gh actions-lock --no-narrow` and never edited by hand) pins those transitive
Actions and records each source repository's identity
([Workflow dependency lockfiles](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles)).
The official GitHub
Dependency Review action evaluates manifest and lockfile changes on every pull
request to `main`, and the Pages workflow installs the committed lockfile with lifecycle
scripts disabled.

Documentation-only repair of two passages left inaccurate by the lockfile-adoption change (#160), without touching workflows, pins, the lockfile or the master instruction text.

The previous wording stated a rule the repository does not follow (the Actions inventory does embed commits in license links) and understated the scope of a shipped change, which would mislead the next dependency-bump sweep of Sections 6.E and 7.A.
